newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares rise on central bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares rise on central bank rate cut.

text.p: Delhi shares opened higher on Thursday, buoyed by a Reserve Bank of India decision to cut the bank rate, the rate at which banks borrow from the central bank, by one percentage point, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange sensitive index rose 2.23 points to 868.47.
"The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) reducing the interest rate by one percent cheered the capital market," said Maninder Singh of brokers Virat Financial Consultants.
RBI on Wednesday cut the bank rate by one percentage point to 10 percent per annum.
"Share prices were higher last evening in kerb trading after the news was announced," Singh said.
Reliance Industries rose 2.05 rupees to 367.50 ahead of a meeting by the firm's board to consider a bonus issue.
State Bank of India rose 3.35 rupees to 343.
